title: Inverse image of etale sheaves of modules over a constant ring is exact
statement: Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $R$ a commutative ring, $R_U$ and $R_V$ the constant sheaves of rings with value $R$ on the small etale sites $U_{\Et}$, $V_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)=\Mod(R_T)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\to\Ab(U_{\Et})$ be the inverse image of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $u^{-1}$ also the inverse image of sheaves of sets and of rings [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. Then: (1) the inverse image of the sheaf of rings $R_V$ is canonically isomorphic to $R_U$: the morphism of sheaves of rings $c:u^{-1}R_V\to R_U$ adjoint to the map $\gamma:R_V\to u_*R_U$ induced, by the universal property of sheafification, by the constant sections $R\to R_U(U\times_VW)$, is an isomorphism; (2) for a sheaf $G$ of $R_V$-modules, $u^{-1}G$ carries a unique structure of sheaf of $u^{-1}R_V$-modules, hence of $R_U$-modules through (1), such that $u^{-1}$ of the action map is the action map; this defines a functor $u^{-1}:\Mod(V_{\Et},R)\to\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ compatible with $u^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves under the forgetful functors, equal (up to a canonical isomorphism natural in $G$) to the module pullback $u^*G=u^{-1}G\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V}R_U$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; (3) this functor is additive and exact (it preserves finite limits and finite colimits), and it is left adjoint to the direct image $u_*:\Mod(U_{\Et},R)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$, $(u_*F)(W)=F(U\times_VW)$ with $R_V$ acting through $\gamma$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the unit and counit being those of the adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ on abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact): f^{-1} is exact on abelian sheaves and f^* is exact for a flat morphism of ringed topoi; here u is flat as a morphism of ringed sites because u^{-1}R_V -> R_U is an isomorphism (constant sheaves: sites.tex Example 0H7J, Mor(E, F) = Map(E, Gamma(F))); used in sites-cohomology.tex Section 0735 (section-base-change-map) for flat pullback on D^+

proof.text: *(1) The constant ring.* The final object of $V_{\Et}$ is $\mathrm{id}:V\to V$ and that of $U_{\Et}$ is $\mathrm{id}:U\to U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $U\times_VV=U$, so for a sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$ we have $\Gamma(V_{\Et},u_*F)=(u_*F)(V)=F(U)=\Gamma(U_{\Et},F)$, naturally in $F$. Let $F$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $U_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] (2) (adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ on sheaves of rings) and by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections] (for rings) applied on $V_{\Et}$ and on $U_{\Et}$ we get bijections, each natural in $F$: $\operatorname{Hom}(u^{-1}R_V,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R_V,u_*F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(R,(u_*F)(V))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(R,F(U))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R_U,F)$. By the Yoneda lemma (in the category of sheaves of commutative rings on $U_{\Et}$) there is a unique isomorphism of sheaves of rings $c:u^{-1}R_V\to R_U$ such that this composite bijection is $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ c$. To identify $c$, take $F=R_U$ and $\psi=\mathrm{id}$: the composite sends $\mathrm{id}_{R_U}$ to the ring map $c_R:R\to R_U(U)$, $r\mapsto$ the constant section $r$, which corresponds to the morphism $\gamma:R_V\to u_*R_U$ with $\gamma_V\circ c^V_R=c_R$; by naturality of the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections] under restriction, $\gamma_W$ sends the image of the constant section $r$ to the constant section $r$ of $R_U(U\times_VW)$, i.e. $\gamma$ is the map induced by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] from the constant presheaf maps $R\to R_U(U\times_VW)$; and $c$ is the adjoint of $\gamma$, i.e. $c=\varepsilon_{R_U}\circ u^{-1}\gamma$. So the morphism $c$ of the statement is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] (2), (3) it is also an isomorphism of the underlying abelian sheaves, $u^{-1}R_V$ being computed by the abelian inverse image.

proof.text: *(2) The module structure.* Let $G$ be a sheaf of $R_V$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with action $\mu:R_V\times G\to G$, a morphism of sheaves of sets. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] (1) $u^{-1}$ commutes with finite products, so $u^{-1}\mu$ is a morphism $u^{-1}R_V\times u^{-1}G=u^{-1}(R_V\times G)\to u^{-1}G$; by (2) of that lemma the ring and group structures of $u^{-1}R_V$ and $u^{-1}G$ are $u^{-1}$ of those of $R_V$ and $G$. The module axioms (associativity $\mu\circ(m\times\mathrm{id})=\mu\circ(\mathrm{id}\times\mu)$, unit, the two distributivity laws) are equalities between morphisms out of finite products built from $\mu$ and the structure maps; applying the functor $u^{-1}$, which preserves finite products and projections, gives the same equalities for $u^{-1}\mu$. So $u^{-1}G$ is a sheaf of $u^{-1}R_V$-modules with action $u^{-1}\mu$, and this structure is unique with that property since the action map is prescribed. Transporting along the ring isomorphism $c$ of step 1, $R_U$ acts by $u^{-1}\mu\circ(c^{-1}\times\mathrm{id})$. If $\varphi:G\to G'$ is $R_V$-linear, i.e. $\mu'\circ(\mathrm{id}\times\varphi)=\varphi\circ\mu$, applying $u^{-1}$ shows that $u^{-1}\varphi$ is $u^{-1}R_V$-linear, hence $R_U$-linear; so $u^{-1}$ is a functor $\Mod(V_{\Et},R)\to\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$. Its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$, and on morphisms it is the abelian $u^{-1}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] (2), (3): $\mathrm{forget}\circ u^{-1}=u^{-1}\circ\mathrm{forget}$ (up to the canonical isomorphism of (3)).

*(2) Equality with the module pullback.* The module pullback of $(u,c)$ is $u^*G=u^{-1}G\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V}R_U$, the change of rings along $c$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], i.e. the sheafification of the presheaf $W\mapsto u^{-1}G(W)\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V(W)}R_U(W)$. Since each $c_W:u^{-1}R_V(W)\to R_U(W)$ is a ring isomorphism, the map $u^{-1}G(W)\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V(W)}R_U(W)\to u^{-1}G(W)$, $x\otimes a\mapsto c_W^{-1}(a)x$, is an isomorphism of $R_U(W)$-modules with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ (for an $A$-module $M$ and a ring isomorphism $A\to A'$, $M\otimes_AA'\cong M$), compatible with the restriction maps and natural in $G$. So the presheaf tensor product is isomorphic to the sheaf $u^{-1}G$ with the $R_U$-module structure of step 2, and the sheafification of a presheaf isomorphic to a sheaf is that sheaf (the isomorphism satisfies the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]). Hence $u^*G\cong u^{-1}G$ as sheaves of $R_U$-modules, naturally in $G$.

*(3) Additivity and exactness.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (1) the forgetful functor $\mathrm{forget}:\Mod(R_T)\to\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels; the addition of morphisms in $\Mod(R_T)$ is the sectionwise addition, that of $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] the abelian $u^{-1}$ is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels. Additivity: $\mathrm{forget}(u^{-1}(\varphi+\psi))=u^{-1}(\mathrm{forget}\varphi+\mathrm{forget}\psi)=\mathrm{forget}(u^{-1}\varphi)+\mathrm{forget}(u^{-1}\psi)$ by step 2, and $\mathrm{forget}$ is faithful and additive. Kernels: let $\varphi:G\to G'$ be a morphism of $\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$ with kernel $k:K\to G$. Then $\mathrm{forget}(k)$ is a kernel of $\mathrm{forget}(\varphi)$, so $u^{-1}\mathrm{forget}(k)=\mathrm{forget}(u^{-1}k)$ is a kernel of $\mathrm{forget}(u^{-1}\varphi)$; the comparison morphism $\kappa:u^{-1}K\to\ker(u^{-1}\varphi)$ in $\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ becomes, after $\mathrm{forget}$ (which preserves the kernel on the right), a morphism between two kernels of the same map compatible with the inclusions, hence an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. A morphism of sheaves of $R_U$-modules whose components are bijective has $R_U(W)$-linear inverse components (the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear), so $\kappa$ is an isomorphism in $\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$: $u^{-1}$ preserves kernels. The same argument with cokernels (or step 5 below and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]) shows that $u^{-1}$ preserves cokernels. An additive functor preserves the zero object and finite direct sums (= finite products and coproducts), and preserving kernels (resp. cokernels) it preserves equalizers $\ker(f-g)$ (resp. coequalizers $\operatorname{coker}(f-g)$); as every finite limit (colimit) is built from a final (initial) object, binary products (coproducts) and equalizers (coequalizers), $u^{-1}:\Mod(V_{\Et},R)\to\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ commutes with finite limits and finite colimits, i.e. is exact.

source.place: Lemma 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact): f^{-1} exact on abelian sheaves; here f^* = f^{-1} (step 3) and exactness is read off on the underlying abelian sheaves

proof.text: *(3) The adjunction.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction] with $\mathcal O=R_V$: for a sheaf of $R_V$-modules $G$ and a sheaf of $u^{-1}R_V$-modules $F$, a morphism of abelian sheaves $u^{-1}G\to F$ is $u^{-1}R_V$-linear iff its adjoint $G\to u_*F$ is $R_V$-linear, where $R_V$ acts on $u_*F$ through $R_V\xrightarrow{\eta}u_*u^{-1}R_V$. Let now $F$ be a sheaf of $R_U$-modules, regarded as a $u^{-1}R_V$-module through the isomorphism $c$ of step 1. A morphism $u^{-1}G\to F$ is $R_U$-linear iff it is $u^{-1}R_V$-linear, both module structures being transported along $c$ (step 2). The resulting $R_V$-module structure on $u_*F$ is restriction along $u_*c\circ\eta_{R_V}:R_V\to u_*R_U$, which is the adjoint of $c$, i.e. $\gamma$ (step 1): so $R_V(W)$ acts on $(u_*F)(W)=F(U\times_VW)$ through $\gamma_W$, the image of the constant section $r$ acting as the constant section $r$ of $R_U(U\times_VW)$, which is the $R_V$-module structure of the direct image $u_*F$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Hence the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ab}(u^{-1}G,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ab}(G,u_*F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] restricts to a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_U}(u^{-1}G,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_V}(G,u_*F)$, natural in $G$ and $F$ (naturality is inherited from the abelian adjunction, the forgetful functors being faithful), whose unit and counit are the abelian ones (linear by the same lemma). So $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ on $\Mod(-,R)$; with steps 3 and 4 this is the module pullback $u^*$ of the morphism of ringed sites $(u,c)$, a flat one since $c$ is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks sites-modules 03D2/03D3/03D6/03D7/04JC and sites 0H7J. The abelian inverse image of def-weil-pbc-inverse-image cannot carry the bilinear action map or the ring structure, so a new node (lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures, Stacks 00X6/00YV) supplies u^{-1} on sheaves of sets and rings, exact, compatible with the abelian one. Step 1: u^{-1}R_V = R_U by Yoneda from the adjunction and the constant-sheaf adjunction (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections = constantSheafAdj). Step 2: module structure (03D2), compatibility with forget. Step 3: u^* = u^{-1} since the change of rings is along an isomorphism. Step 4: additive and exact through the faithful exact forgetful functor (lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful) and prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact. Step 5: adjunction from the new node lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction (03D3), with the R_V-structure on u_*F identified as restriction along gamma. Statement clarified (not changed in substance): the map c and gamma are named, the set/ring inverse image, the tensor product and the direct image are cited, and it is said that unit and counit are the abelian ones (used by lem-weil-pbc-retract-supplied).
